mainTopic: How far רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון each take their positions on שחיטה שאינה ראויה (a slaughter that cannot make the animal permitted, like slaughtering a טרפה), and whether רבי מאיר's view could let a living fetus found inside a slaughtered טרפה skip its own שחיטה.
overview: The amud opens with a statement that limits both sides of an argument about שחיטה שאינה ראויה, a slaughter that cannot make the animal permitted, like slaughtering a טרפה. רבי מאיר says it still counts as שחיטה, but he agrees it does not permit eating. רבי שמעון says it does not count, but he agrees it removes the טומאה of נבלה. For each half the גמרא asks why it is needed, and it finds a case where the point is not obvious. For רבי מאיר's half, the case is a living fetus found inside a slaughtered טרפה, and the statement turns out to be needed for רבי, who mixes רבי מאיר's view with the רבנן's view. For רבי שמעון's half, the case is a non-sacred טרפה slaughtered in the עזרה, where he permits benefit. רב פפא and אביי then prove from a משנה that רבי שמעון treats the ban on חולין בעזרה as Torah law, since we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. The amud ends with a story: רבי told רבי חייא to use a bird's blood to drive moths from his flax. The גמרא asks how this fits the rule of covering the blood, and it begins to examine רבי's own view of bird slaughter, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון have limits to their positions
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי מאיר, who says a 'useless' slaughter counts as שחיטה, agrees it does not make the meat kosher. Even רבי שמעון, who says it does not count, agrees it removes נבלה impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר did not mean for every law that a slaughter which cannot permit the animal still counts as שחיטה. He agrees it does not make the meat permitted to eat. And רבי שמעון did not mean for every law that such a slaughter does not count. He agrees it makes the animal pure from the טומאה of נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that sets limits on both sides of the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון about שחיטה שאינה ראויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says a slaughter that cannot permit the meat (for example, slaughtering a טרפה) still has the legal name 'שחיטה', and רבי שמעון says it does not. This statement shows neither goes all the way. For רבי מאיר it still cannot permit eating, and for רבי שמעון it still prevents the carcass from having the impurity of a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughter that is not 'fit', meaning it cannot make the animal permitted to eat, such as slaughtering a טרפה.
It is legally called a slaughter and counts as one.
He agrees or concedes.
An animal with a fatal defect. It is forbidden to eat even if slaughtered properly.
An animal that died without proper שחיטה. It is forbidden and passes on טומאה.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: it counts as שחיטה, but it never permits eating. רבי שמעון: it does not count as שחיטה, but it still removes נבלה impurity.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי שמעון holds the slaughtered טרפה is a נבלה. He agrees the slaughter does remove the נבלה impurity, even though he says it is not called שחיטה for other laws.

phrases.english: Not with regard to everything did Rabbi Meir say
that a slaughter which is not fit is considered a slaughter;
phrases.notes: 'Not fit' means the slaughter can't make the animal kosher, like slaughtering a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir agrees
that it does not permit it for eating;
and not with regard to everything did Rabbi Shimon say

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה:
phrases.english: that a slaughter which is not fit is not considered a slaughter;
Rabbi Shimon agrees
that it makes it pure from the impurity of a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא לַכֹּל אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by stating the limits of each view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי מאיר, a 'useless' slaughter counts as שחיטה but does not permit eating. Under רבי שמעון, it does not count as שחיטה but still removes נבלה impurity.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר's concession need to be said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's half of the statement again and asks why it is needed. Obviously slaughter can't make a טרפה kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said that רבי מאיר agrees such a slaughter does not permit the meat for eating. But that is obvious! Can a טרפה ever become permitted through slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי מאיר's half of the statement and challenges it as obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a טרפה is forbidden even after a perfect שחיטה. So saying that רבי מאיר agrees it isn't permitted seems to teach nothing new. The גמרא wants to find what the statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! A challenge that a statement teaches nothing new.
Does it become permitted?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: לֹא לַכֹּל אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: The master said: Not with regard to everything did Rabbi Meir say
that a slaughter which is not fit is considered a slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁאֵין מַתִּירָתָהּ בַּאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir agrees that it does not permit it for eating.
That's obvious!
Does a טרפה become permitted through slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: לֹא לַכֹּל אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of the statement in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's concession that a 'useless' slaughter does not permit eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה can never become permitted by שחיטה, so the concession seems obvious and unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is a living fetus found inside a slaughtered טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The statement teaches that when a טרפה is slaughtered and a live nine-month fetus is found inside, the mother's slaughter does not permit the fetus. It needs its own שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for someone who slaughtered a טרפה and found a living nine-month fetus inside it. You might have thought: since רבי מאיר says a 'useless' slaughter still counts as שחיטה, the mother's slaughter should work for the fetus, and the fetus shouldn't need its own slaughter. So the statement teaches us that it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the statement is not about the mother's meat. It is about a living fetus found inside her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the שחיטה of a kosher mother can permit the fetus inside her. Since רבי מאיר says the slaughter of a טרפה still 'counts', one could think it would at least permit the fetus. The statement 'it does not permit eating' tells us it permits nothing, so the fetus is not permitted through its mother either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case. Used to show a statement is not obvious.
A living, fully developed nine-month fetus.
You might have thought. Introduces the mistaken assumption.
The slaughter of its mother.
It teaches us. The new point the statement adds.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי מאיר's 'it counts as שחיטה' does not extend to permitting anything for eating, not even the fetus.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for one who slaughters a טרפה
and found inside it a living nine-month fetus;
it would enter your mind to say:
since Rabbi Meir said:
a slaughter which is not fit is considered a slaughter,
let the slaughter of its mother work for it
and it should not need its own slaughter,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לְשׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the statement to a specific, non-obvious case (the fetus).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the slaughter of a טרפה 'counts' for רבי מאיר, it might permit the live fetus inside without its own שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother's 'useless' slaughter does not permit the fetus. It needs its own שחיטה.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר requires שחיטה even for a בן פקועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי מאיר holds that even a fetus taken from a properly slaughtered kosher mother needs its own שחיטה, so how could anyone think the slaughter of a טרפה would exempt it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think so? Didn't רבי מאיר say that a בן פקועה needs its own שחיטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'you might have thought' of step 3. Under רבי מאיר, that mistake could never have arisen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן פקועה is a fetus removed from a mother that was properly slaughtered. רבי מאיר says it still needs its own שחיטה. If even a kosher mother's slaughter doesn't exempt the fetus, the slaughter of a טרפה surely wouldn't. So the statement still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? Introduces a challenge to the assumption just made.
A fetus found in an animal that was properly slaughtered.
Requires slaughter.

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge targets the answer in step 3, not the original statement directly. The גמרא is saying that the 'you might have thought' could not happen under רבי מאיר's own view.

phrases.english: And do you really think so?
But didn't Rabbi Meir say:
a בן פקועה requires slaughter!
phrases.notes: This is a fetus from a properly slaughtered, kosher mother. Even then, רבי מאיר wants it slaughtered on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'you might have thought' in step 3, that the mother's slaughter could exempt the fetus under רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר requires שחיטה even for a בן פקועה of a kosher mother. So nobody would think the slaughter of a טרפה exempts the fetus, and the statement is again unnecessary.

steps.title: The statement is needed for רבי, who agrees partly with רבי מאיר and partly with the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the statement is not needed for רבי מאיר himself. It is needed for רבי, who holds like רבי מאיר that an unfit slaughter counts as שחיטה, and like the רבנן that the mother's slaughter makes the fetus kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רבי. רבי agrees with רבי מאיר that a slaughter which cannot make the meat kosher still counts as a slaughter. He also agrees with the רבנן that slaughtering the mother makes the fetus inside her kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4. The statement was never needed for רבי מאיר himself; it is needed for רבי, who mixes two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked: רבי מאיר says a fetus always needs its own שחיטה, so why teach it about a טרפה? The answer moves the statement to רבי. He holds like רבי מאיר that an unfit slaughter still 'counts', but like the רבנן that a mother's slaughter covers her fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (for the obvious case); it is needed for a different case
The Sages, the majority opinion against רבי מאיר
Slaughtering the mother makes the fetus inside her kosher
A slaughter that cannot make the meat kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, a different person from רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: It is not needed [for רבי מאיר himself];
for Rabbi holds like רבי מאיר
and he also holds like the Rabbis.
He holds like רבי מאיר, who says:
a slaughter that is not fit is still called a slaughter,
and he holds like the Rabbis, who say:
the slaughter of its mother makes it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּרַבִּי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 by shifting whose opinion the statement is for.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the statement to a different authority (רבי) who combines two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement seemed pointless because רבי מאיר requires שחיטה for every fetus anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement is needed for רבי, whose mixed position could have misled us.

steps.title: Why we might have thought the fetus needs no slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי holds like the רבנן that the mother's slaughter makes the fetus kosher, we might have thought this works even when the mother is a טרפה. The statement teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the רבנן say the mother's slaughter makes the fetus kosher, you might think that for רבי the slaughter of a טרפה mother also works for the fetus, so the fetus would not need its own שחיטה. The statement teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by spelling out the mistake we might have made without the statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put רבי's two views together: an unfit slaughter still counts, and a mother's slaughter covers her fetus. Then slaughtering a טרפה mother should cover the fetus too. The statement blocks this: for a טרפה mother, the fetus still needs its own שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (something we would not have known)
Let it be effective for it

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, slaughtering a טרפה counts as 'slaughter', but it does not make the fetus inside kosher. The fetus needs its own שחיטה.

phrases.english: Since the Rabbis said
the slaughter of its mother makes it fit,
let the slaughter of its mother work for it [even for a טרפה]
and it should not need its own slaughter;
so it teaches us [that it does need slaughter].

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of Step 5 by stating the mistake it prevents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mistaken assumption the statement comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי, the slaughter of a טרפה mother would free the fetus from needing שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for רבי, the fetus of a slaughtered טרפה needs its own שחיטה.

steps.title: Isn't רבי שמעון's agreement obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of the statement: רבי שמעון agrees that slaughtering a טרפה removes נבלה status. It asks why this is needed, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The statement said: רבי שמעון did not say for every purpose that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter. He agrees that it saves the animal from being impure as a נבלה. The גמרא asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of רבי אבא's statement, about רבי שמעון. It asks why it needs to be said at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 2, where the גמרא asked the same question about the רבי מאיר half. Here the claim is that a slaughtered טרפה is not נבלה. The גמרא says that is too obvious to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it makes people and things impure
Agrees, concedes

phrases.english: And not for all purposes did רבי שמעון say

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: that a slaughter which is not fit is not called a slaughter;
רבי שמעון agrees
that it makes the animal pure from the status of נבלה.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא לַכֹּל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי מאיר half of the statement to the רבי שמעון half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second half of רבי אבא's statement, about רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement that teaches nothing new is pointless, and this law already seems known.

steps.title: A פסוק already teaches that a slaughtered טרפה is not נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves it is obvious. From the word 'מן' in the פסוק, רב (or a ברייתא) learns that some animals do not make things impure as נבלה, namely a טרפה that was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say a ברייתא taught: 'And if one of the animals dies.' The word 'of' teaches that some animals make things impure and some do not. Which one does not? A טרפה that was slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its 'obvious!' challenge. It shows that a slaughtered טרפה not being נבלה is already learned from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' ('of') suggests only part of the animals: some dead animals make things impure and some do not. The ones that do not are טרפות that were slaughtered. Since this is already known from the פסוק, רבי אבא's statement seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים (here, a ברייתא)
Some, a part of
Makes impure
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after שחיטה

phrases.english: For רב יהודה said that רב said,
and some say it was taught in a ברייתא:
"And if there dies of the animals" —
some animals make things impure
and some animals do not make things impure;
and which is this? A טרפה that one slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source showing why the point in Step 7 is obvious.
steps.raayaObject: That a slaughtered טרפה is not impure as נבלה, so the statement adds nothing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'וכי ימות מן הבהמה' (ויקרא 11:39), as taught by רב or a ברייתא

steps.title: The statement is needed for a טרפה slaughtered as חולין in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the statement is needed for someone who slaughters a non-sacred טרפה inside the עזרה. There רבי שמעון holds the slaughter does not count, yet it still removes נבלה status.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for someone who slaughters a טרפה that is a non-sacred animal inside the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious!' challenge by pointing to a special case where the statement teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the next step we see that רבי שמעון holds that slaughtering a טרפה in the עזרה does not count as forbidden 'slaughter'. Since he treats it as 'no slaughter' there, we might think it does not count for נבלה either. The statement teaches that it still removes נבלה status.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-sacred animal slaughtered inside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
The Temple courtyard

phrases.english: No, it is needed for one who slaughters a טרפה
and it is a non-sacred animal in the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לְשׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה וְהִיא חוּלִּין בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious!' challenge of Steps 7–8 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the statement in a specific case where it teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since for רבי שמעון the slaughter does not count in the עזרה, it might not count for removing נבלה status either.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in that case, רבי שמעון agrees the slaughter removes נבלה status.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי שמעון permits benefit from a טרפה slaughtered in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון permits benefit from a non-sacred טרפה slaughtered in the עזרה, because for him that slaughter does not count. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: if someone slaughters a טרפה, or slaughters an animal that turns out to be a טרפה, and either one was a non-sacred animal in the Temple courtyard, רבי שמעון permits getting benefit from it, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the case in Step 9. It shows that רבי שמעון treats a טרפה's slaughter in the עזרה as 'not a slaughter'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a non-sacred animal slaughtered in the עזרה is forbidden for any benefit. רבי שמעון permits it here because a טרפה's slaughter does not count, so no forbidden slaughter happened. That is why רבי אבא had to say that רבי שמעון still agrees it removes נבלה status.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit, use (for example, selling it or feeding it to animals)
Permits
And the Sages forbid
It was found to be a טרפה (discovered only after slaughter)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, slaughtering a טרפה does not count as 'slaughter' for the ban on חולין בעזרה, but it does count for removing נבלה impurity.

phrases.english: As it was taught: one who slaughters a טרפה,
and likewise one who slaughters and it was found to be a טרפה,
in both cases non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard —
רבי שמעון permits them for benefit,
and the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה, וְכֵן הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִמְצֵאת טְרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the case named in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון treats the slaughter of a טרפה in the עזרה as not a slaughter
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the חכמים

steps.title: Why the statement is needed even for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that since רבי שמעון permits benefit, the slaughter counts for nothing and the animal stays a נבלה. The statement teaches that it still removes נבלה status.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since רבי שמעון says benefit is permitted, it clearly is not a slaughter at all. So say it does not remove נבלה status either. The statement teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 9. It spells out the mistake we would have made without this statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits benefit because, for him, slaughtering a טרפה (even a non-sacred one in the עזרה) is not a real שחיטה. From that we might conclude it cannot remove נבלה status either. The statement teaches that it does: the slaughter does not count for the עזרה ban, but it still works to remove נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
It teaches us (the point the statement makes)
Permitted to benefit from it
Makes it pure (removes its impurity)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, slaughtering a non-sacred טרפה in the עזרה does not count as שחיטה when it comes to the עזרה ban, yet it still removes the animal's נבלה impurity.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two results. 'Not a real slaughter' explains why benefit is permitted. It does not mean the animal stays an impure נבלה.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה,
phrases.english: Since Rabbi Shimon said: it is permitted for benefit,
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא in step 10 about a non-sacred טרפה slaughtered in the עזרה.

phrases.english: evidently it is not a slaughter at all,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: מִידֵי נְבֵלָה נָמֵי לָא מְטַהֲרָה,
phrases.english: so say: it also does not make it pure from נבלה status,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 10 to spell out the mistaken first idea that the statement rules out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a real mistaken first idea (הוה אמינא) that makes the statement necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the slaughter does not count for the עזרה ban, it also would not remove נבלה status.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for רבי שמעון, the slaughter removes נבלה status.

steps.title: Is the ban on non-sacred animals in the עזרה a Torah law for רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי whether רבי שמעון holds that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are forbidden by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Does רבי שמעון really hold that חולין בעזרה is forbidden by Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: A side question opens. רב פפא wants to know how strong רבי שמעון's ban on חולין בעזרה is: Torah law or rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion so far assumed that רבי שמעון treats this slaughter as 'not a real slaughter'. That would make sense if he holds the ban comes from the Torah. רב פפא asks whether this is really his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard
From the Torah (Torah law)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
And does Rabbi Shimon hold
that non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard are forbidden by Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the level of the ban mentioned in רבי שמעון's position from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון holds the ban on חולין בעזרה is from the Torah or from the רבנן.

steps.title: אביי says yes and quotes a משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers yes. He quotes a משנה where רבי שמעון says חולין slaughtered in the עזרה must be burned, and so must a חיה slaughtered there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. We learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון says, non-sacred animals slaughtered in the עזרה must be burned in fire, and so must a wild animal slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his answer, and he brings a משנה as the basis for his proof. The next step explains how this משנה proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is the extra clause about a חיה. רבי שמעון forbids not only a בהמה slaughtered in the עזרה but also a חיה. אביי will use this extra clause to show that the בהמה ban must come from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
They must be burned in fire (no benefit allowed)
Wild (undomesticated) animal, like a deer

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
and we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard
shall be burned in fire,
and likewise a wild animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, וְהָתְנַן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question and brings the source for the answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, רבי שמעון holds it is Torah law, based on his ruling in the משנה.

steps.title: The חיה ban proves the בהמה ban is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: Burning a חיה is a fence around the בהמה ban. If the בהמה ban were only rabbinic, the חיה ban would be a fence around a fence, which the רבנן do not make. So the בהמה ban must be from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the ban is from the Torah, that explains why we forbid a חיה because of a בהמה. But if you say the ban is rabbinic, why is a בהמה forbidden? Because someone might come to eat קדשים outside. That itself is a גזירה. Would we then add a גזירה on top of a גזירה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how the משנה proves his answer. He compares two options, Torah law or rabbinic law, and shows that only Torah law fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בהמה ban is Torah law, forbidding a חיה is an ordinary rabbinic fence so people do not confuse the two. If the בהמה ban were itself rabbinic, made so people would not come to eat קדשים outside, then the חיה ban would be a fence around a fence. Since the רבנן do not make a גזירה לגזירה, the בהמה ban must come from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say...
We make a rabbinic ban because of (a fence around) something else
Sacrificial meat eaten outside its proper place
A fence on top of a fence, which the רבנן do not make

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are forbidden by Torah law. The proof is that he also forbids a חיה, and that extra ban only makes sense as a fence around a Torah law, since we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This backs up the earlier steps. Because רבי שמעון treats חולין בעזרה as Torah law, he can say such a slaughter 'does not count' for the עזרה ban, while it still removes נבלה status.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is forbidden by Torah law,
that is why we decree on a wild animal because of a domesticated animal.
But if you say it is rabbinic,
then for a domesticated animal, what is the reason?
Lest one come to eat sacrificial meat outside,
that itself is a decree,
and will we get up and make a decree for a decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 13 proves the ban is from the Torah.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds the ban on חולין בעזרה is from the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי שמעון also burns a חיה slaughtered in the עזרה, together with the rule that we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: Moths in רבי חייא's flax
steps.stepSummary: Moths got into רבי חייא's flax. רבי told him to slaughter a bird over the water tub, because the moths would smell the blood and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moths fell into רבי חייא's flax. He came before רבי, who told him: Take a bird and slaughter it over the tub of water, because the moths will smell the blood and leave the flax.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a story about getting rid of moths by slaughtering a bird over water. The story sets up a discussion about covering the bird's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood falls into the water tub, so it is not being handled in the usual way for a bird's blood. The story is told as the opening of the next discussion, which picks up on this detail.

keyTerms.meaning: Moths or similar small pests
Flax
A tub of water (where the flax was soaked)
A bird

phrases.english: For Rabbi Ḥiyya, there fell
moths into his flax,
he came before Rabbi,
he said to him: Take a bird
and slaughter it over the tub of water,
for they will smell the blood and leave it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא נְפַל לֵיהּ יָאנִיבָא בְּכִיתָּנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and opens a new topic with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי advised slaughtering a bird over a water tub so the smell of blood would drive the moths from the flax.

steps.title: How could רבי חייא use the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story of רבי חייא from a ברייתא. Someone who slaughters because he needs the blood must still cover it. He should stab the animal or tear out its throat instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? A ברייתא teaches: if someone slaughters because he needs the blood, he still has to cover it. So what should he do? Either stab it or tear out its throat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the advice from step 15. Slaughtering a bird and then using its blood seems to break the rule of covering the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper שחיטה of a bird creates a duty to cover the blood, even if you wanted the blood for something else. The ברייתא says the way around this is to kill the animal without a real שחיטה, by stabbing it or tearing out its throat. רבי told רבי חייא to slaughter, so the blood should have needed covering.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal (חיה)
Needs the blood for some use
Stabbing or piercing the throat, which is not a kosher slaughter
Tearing the windpipe and gullet out instead of cutting them

phrases.english: How could he do this?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי חייא, who slaughtered a bird and used its blood to drive away the moths.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who slaughters and needs the blood
is obligated to cover it.
So how should he act?
Either he stabs it or he tears out its throat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story told in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's instruction to רבי חייא to slaughter a bird and use its blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires covering the blood even when the slaughterer needs it. It says to stab or tear the animal instead. So slaughtering in order to use the blood seems forbidden.

steps.title: Two reports of what רבי really said
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי said 'Go make it a טרפה.' רבין reports that he said 'Go stab it.' Either way, there is no duty to cover the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי told him 'Go make it a טרפה.' When רבין came, he said: רבי told him 'Go stab it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבי never told him to do a plain שחיטה. Two rabbis give two versions of what he actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב דימי's version, the bird is first made a טרפה, and slaughtering a טרפה does not require covering the blood. In רבין's version, רבי simply told him to stab the bird, which matches the ברייתא's advice. Both versions remove the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury, which may not be eaten even if slaughtered
Go and make it a טרפה (injure it fatally first)
Go and stab it

phrases.english: When רב דימי came, he said:
"Go make it a טרפה," is what he told him.
When רבין came, he said:
"Go stab it," is what he told him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by correcting what רבי actually said
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the story: רבי's instruction was not a plain שחיטה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי told רבי חייא to do a normal שחיטה, which would require covering the blood
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי told him either to make the bird a טרפה first (רב דימי) or to stab it (רבין). In both cases no covering is needed.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי just say 'stab it'?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב דימי's version, the גמרא asks why רבי gave the more roundabout advice instead of simply saying 'stab it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'Go make it a טרפה,' why didn't רבי just say 'Go stab it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רב דימי's version. It wants to know why רבי picked the טרפה method over stabbing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly offers stabbing as the solution. So it seems odd that רבי would choose to make the bird a טרפה and then slaughter it. The גמרא looks for a reason why stabbing would not work in רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
What is the reason?

phrases.english: According to the one who says "Go make it a טרפה,"
what is the reason he did not say "Go stab it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״צֵא טְרוֹף״, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר ״צֵא נְחוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first of the two versions given in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי, in רב דימי's version, did not use the simpler method of stabbing that the ברייתא suggests

steps.title: A suggested reason: birds need no Torah slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי holds birds have no Torah requirement of שחיטה. If so, stabbing a bird would count as its 'slaughter,' and the blood would need covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he holds that a bird does not need שחיטה by Torah law, so stabbing it counts as its slaughter...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to step 18. It sets this answer up so it can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah gives no special slaughter rule for birds, then any way of killing a bird, including stabbing, counts as its 'שחיטה.' Then stabbing would also create a duty to cover the blood. That would explain why רבי chose the טרפה method instead.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
He holds (this view)
By Torah law, a bird has no required way of slaughter

phrases.english: And if you would say that he holds
that there is no slaughter required for a bird by Torah law,
and so stabbing it is its slaughter,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, קָסָבַר אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested reason based on רבי's view of bird slaughter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stabbing a bird avoids covering the blood, so רבי should have suggested it
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי holds birds need no Torah slaughter, so stabbing counts as slaughter and still requires covering

steps.title: רבי himself says משה was taught bird slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. A ברייתא shows that רבי learns from the פסוק 'as I have commanded you' that משה was taught exact slaughter rules, including for birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי says: 'As I have commanded you' teaches that משה was commanded about the gullet and the windpipe, about cutting most of one of them in a bird, and most of both of them in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 19. It quotes רבי himself saying that birds do have Torah slaughter rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads 'as I have commanded you' to mean משה received detailed slaughter rules. These include cutting most of one sign (gullet or windpipe) for a bird. So in רבי's view, bird slaughter is from the Torah, stabbing is not slaughter, and the question from step 18 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: "As I have commanded you": the source that משה was taught the rules of שחיטה
Gullet (food pipe)
Windpipe
Most of one sign, the minimum cut for a bird
Most of both signs, the minimum cut for an animal

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי quoted in this ברייתא is the same רבי who advised רבי חייא. That is exactly why his own words can be used against the suggestion.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: רבי says:
"As I have commanded you"
teaches that Moshe was commanded
about the gullet and about the windpipe,
and about cutting most of one of them in a bird,
and about cutting most of both of them in an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested reason from step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the suggested reason; the question of step 18 stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי clearly holds that birds have Torah slaughter rules, so stabbing a bird is not its slaughter
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key source that the details of שחיטה, including the different minimum cuts for birds and animals, were taught to משה as Torah law.
